Subject: Orchid Systems — post-call technical deep-dive & deployment readiness

Hi Elena / Raj —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap while notes are fresh and to confirm next steps so we can scope a focused POC:  

Key pain points you described
- Highly variable latency during weekend marketing bursts (observed spikes to p95 ~700ms even for short prompts)
- Burst throughput requirements during promos (short windows of ~10–15 minutes with 600–900 QPS)
- Need for consistent semantic-retrieval + instruction-following model capabilities (reranking + generation)
- Tight security posture (SOC 2 in progress) and requirement for VPC/private networking for production dataset ingestion

Target goals you gave
- P95 inference latency <= 150ms for 16–64 token prompts during steady-state; acceptable p95 up to 250ms during short burst windows
- Sustained throughput target: 400 QPS normal, burst 800 QPS for up to 15 minutes
- Model fidelity: 1) embedding-based reranking with recall > 0.9 on your benchmark set, 2) instruction following with negligible hallucination on canned prompts

Technical items we covered
- Candidate serving topology: primary us-east active, secondary us-west active-standby for failover; optional eu-west read-only for GDPR-sensitive traffic
- KV prefix caching for repeated conversational contexts to decrease per-token compute on warm sessions
- Routing policy: latency-first for customer-facing endpoints, cost-fallsafe to a quantized variant if Dedicated pool is saturated
- Observability needs: token-level billing traces + per-route p95 dashboards (Redwood Console)

Action items (owners & timing)
1) Orchid: share the sample SLO/benchmark dataset and a small production-ish traffic trace (5–10k requests) — Elena/Raj — by Mon 7/27 — attached link in the sheet.
2) Redwood: provide a POC topology sketch, rough cost estimate for a 4-week POC, and a short runbook for traffic shaping during promo bursts — Karthik — by Mon 7/27 (see attached sketch).
3) Legal/Procurement (Orchid): confirm NDA path and procurement timeline so we can schedule on-prem/VPC options if needed — Elena — by Fri 7/31.
4) Schedule: proposed POC kickoff week of 8/2 — agree?

Attachments: orchid_inference_requirements.xlsx (you should see the SLO worksheet we discussed).

Next steps from my side: I’ll loop Karthik into a short sys-architecture note that sketches our recommended Dedicated pool sizing and the autoscale profile. If that looks good to you we’ll lock a 4-week POC and deliver a baseline performance report at the end.

Thanks — available for a quick follow-up if any of the items above need clarifying.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / Raj —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short technical readout and what I recommend for the POC. (See attached sketch: karchik_deployment_sketch.pdf)

1) Model variants and precision- Baseline: open-instruction model (16-bit) for fidelity checks- POC path: quantized int8 variant for throughput testing — Redwood runtime supports int8/4-bit quantization paths; expect ~2.2x inference throughput improvement vs fp16 with modest quality delta on reranking tasks

2) Serving topology for POC
- Dedicated pool in us-east (primary) with autoscale headroom to 1.2x expected peak (we'll provision GPU instances to handle 900 QPS burst).
- Warm standby in us-west to take over in <30s if capacity issues; optional eu-west read-only for compliance checks.

3) Latency & batching
- To hit p95 <150ms: use short batching windows (8–12ms), request prioritization for interactive endpoints, and KV prefix caching for long-running sessions.
- If we must serve both reranking (embedding) + generation in the same route, we'll split into two paths: embedding microservices (CPU + batched GPU for vector encode) and generation pool (GPU). This reduces tail latency at p95.

4) Autoscaling & admission control
- Implement a two-tier autoscale: fast scale-up for <2 min bursts (pre-warmed nodes) and standard scale for sustained load. Admission control will reject low-priority background jobs during burst windows.

5) Observability & SLO measurement
- We'll enable per-request token traces and export p50/p95/p99 to your Grafana (or Redwood Console) with a synthetic traffic test harness.

Estimated POC footprint (rough)
- 3 x A100-style GPUs (or 4 x L40S quantized nodes) pre-warmed, autoscale to 6 GPUs for 900 QPS burst testing- Network: 10 Gbps E/W for cross-region KV sync

Next steps I will own: finalize the deployment sketch and a simple runbook for the promo-burst simulation. I attached the initial sketch (karthik_deployment_sketch.pdf) and a short command list for your traffic generator.
